Subject: Recap: Performance SLOs and autoscaling (FastPay)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we discussed around latency, throughput and burst behavior: 

Key SLOs you stated:
- Median latency target: 150ms per text-generation request (95th < 350ms)
- Sustained throughput target: 400 requests/sec during peak business hours
- Concurrency: typical 600 concurrent sessions, spikes up to ~1,200 concurrently for <10min windows
- Streaming: low-latency token streaming required for UI responsiveness

Autoscaling & burst needs you flagged:
- Warm pool preferred for sub-60s scale-up to maintain 95th percentile SLOs
- Allow short queuing for non-critical background jobs, but user-facing requests should avoid long queues
- Fallback model (smaller/quantized) acceptable during large-scale surges

Attachments: I attached the SLO worksheet you started (fastpay_slo_requirements.xlsx) — please fill any missing peak windows or percentiles.

Next steps:
1) Dylan to confirm feasibility of warm pools and estimate warm-node costs.
2) Laura to draft a quick mutual action plan and proposed implementation milestones.
3) Marissa/Alex follow-up call next week to review proposed config and pricing.

Proposed slot: Tue 18 Aug, 10am PT — does that work?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Recap: Performance SLOs and autoscaling (FastPay)

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 150ms median is for median tokens across short messages (<=256 tokens). For long-generation flows we have relaxed targets (median ~350ms).
- Peak windows are typically 08:00–10:00 PT and 18:00–19:30 PT on weekdays; see the sheet for hourly breakdown.
- Spikes to 1,200 concurrent are usually <8 minutes, triggered by marketing pushes. Those must not degrade checkout latencies beyond 500ms P95.

We prefer warm pools if cost-effective — keeping a small warm fleet (~10% of baseline capacity) would be ideal. If you can share a rough cost delta for warm pool vs cold scale, that would help in procurement.

We attached a short list of streaming requirements and an example UX trace.

Cheers,
Alex
Head of Engineering | FastPay
alex.johnson@fastpay.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Recap: Performance SLOs and autoscaling (FastPay)

Marissa / Laura — reviewing Alex's clarifications. Technical notes / proposed approach: 

- Warm pool strategy: maintain reserved warm nodes equal to ~12% of baseline GPU capacity to cover 90% of expected short spikes. Warm nodes are kept with model loaded and KV cache primed for common prefixes. Estimated cost delta: +18% on baseline compute for reserved warm pool (ballpark).

- Scale-up times: cold spin-up to attach a GPU + load model currently ~3.5—5 minutes depending on model size; warm pool hits <30s for request-ready readiness because model already loaded and warmed caches.

- Queueing behavior: propose prioritized request queueing with two classes — interactive (user-facing, max queue time 5s) and background (batchable, queue tolerant up to 60s). Under large surge, interactive is routed to warm nodes or smaller quantized variant to hit P95 < 500ms.

- Streaming: continuous-token streaming enabled; we will pin a streaming-optimized kernel path and avoid batching that increases headroom latency. We recommend per-route concurrency caps to avoid thundering herd.

Action items for this thread:
- I will produce a short cost estimate for warm pool vs cold scale by EOD Mon and attach the cost sheet.
- Laura — can you draft the mutual action plan and timeline for the pilot?

Dylan
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_autoscale_design.pdf (design brief)
